title.zh: 卷二十二 列傳第十六: 陸子隆 錢道戢 駱牙
title.en: Volume 22: Lu Zilong, Qian Daoji, Luo Ya
title.raw: 卷二十二 列傳第十六: 陸子隆 錢道戢 駱牙 Volume 22: Lu Zilong, Qian Daoji, Luo Ya

sentences.zh: 陳書卷二十二

translations.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 22
translations.idiomatic: Book of Chen, Volume 22

sentences.zh: 列傳第十六

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Sixteen
translations.idiomatic: Biographies, Part Sixteen

sentences.zh: 陸子隆 錢道戢 駱牙

translations.literal: Lu Zilong; Qian Daoji; Luo Ya
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zilong; Qian Daoji; Luo Ya

sentences.zh: 陸子隆字興世，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Lu Zilong, styled Xingshi, was a native of Wu in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zilong, styled Xingshi, came from Wu in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖敞之，梁嘉興令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Changzhi was Liang magistrate of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Changzhi had been magistrate of Jiaxing under Liang.

sentences.zh: 父悛，封氏令。

translations.literal: His father Quan was magistrate of Feng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Quan was magistrate of Feng.

sentences.zh: 子隆少慷慨，有志功名。

translations.literal: Zilong in youth was generous and high-minded and aspired to merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Zilong was open-handed and ambitious, hungry for achievement and renown.

sentences.zh: 起家東宮直後。

translations.literal: He began his career as a direct attendant in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a direct attendant in the eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，於鄉里聚徒。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he gathered followers in his home district.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled he raised men in his home district.

sentences.zh: 是時張彪為吳郡太守，引為將帥。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Biao was Administrator of Wu commandery and took him on as a commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Biao was then administrator of Wu and made him a field commander.

sentences.zh: 彪徙鎮會稽，子隆隨之。

translations.literal: When Biao moved his garrison to Kuaiji, Zilong followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Biao shifted his headquarters to Kuaiji, Zilong went with him.

sentences.zh: 及世祖討彪，彪將沈泰、吳寶真、申縉等皆降，而子隆力戰敗績，世祖義之，復使領其部曲，板為中兵參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen campaigned against Biao, Biao's generals Shen Tai, Wu Baozhen, Shen Jin, and others all surrendered, but Zilong fought hard and was defeated; Emperor Wen honored his loyalty, had him again lead his old command, and commissioned him military adjutant of the central guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen moved against Biao, Biao's generals Shen Tai, Wu Baozhen, Shen Jin, and the rest surrendered—but Zilong fought on and lost. Emperor Wen admired his constancy, restored him to his old troops, and brevetted him military adjutant of the central guard.

sentences.zh: 歷始豐、永興二縣令。

translations.literal: He served in succession as magistrate of Shifeng and Yongxing counties.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as magistrate of Shifeng and Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 華皎據湘州反，以子隆居其心腹，皎深患之，頻遣使招誘，子隆不從，皎因遣兵攻之，又不能剋。

translations.literal: When Hua Jiao held Xiang province in rebellion, because Zilong lay in his very heartland Jiao deeply feared him and repeatedly sent envoys to win him over; Zilong would not yield, so Jiao sent troops to attack him but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Jiao rebelled and held Xiang province. Zilong sat in his heartland, so Jiao feared him and sent envoys again and again to lure him over. Zilong refused. Jiao then attacked but could not break him.

sentences.zh: 及皎敗於郢州，子隆出兵以襲其後，因與王師相會。

translations.literal: When Jiao was defeated at Yingzhou, Zilong led troops to strike his rear and thereby joined the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiao fell at Yingzhou, Zilong marched out to hit his rear and joined the imperial troops.

sentences.zh: 授持節、通直散騎常侍、都督武州諸軍事，進爵為侯，增邑并前七百戶。

translations.literal: He was given the staff, made Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, and Commander of Military Affairs in Wuzhou; his rank was advanced to marquis and his fief increased together with the previous to seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He received the staff, was made regular attendant of direct communication and commander of military affairs in Wuzhou, was raised to marquis, and his fief was brought to seven hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 尋遷都督荊信祐三州諸軍事、宣毅將軍、荊州刺史，持節、常侍如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Commander of Military Affairs in the three provinces of Jing, Xin, and You, made Manifest Resolution General and Inspector of Jing, the staff and regular attendant unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made commander of Jing, Xin, and You, manifest-resolution general and inspector of Jing, keeping the staff and his attendant title.

sentences.zh: 是時荊州新置，治于公安，城池未固，子隆修建城郭，綏集夷夏，甚得民和，當時號為稱職。

translations.literal: At that time Jing province had been newly established, with its seat at Gong'an; the walls were not yet secure; Zilong built the ramparts, soothed and gathered Chinese and barbarians alike, won the people's hearts exceedingly, and at the time was acclaimed as fulfilling his charge.
translations.idiomatic: Jing province was new then, with its seat at Gong'an and its walls still weak. Zilong raised the fortifications, settled Chinese and non-Chinese alike, and won deep goodwill. Men of the day called him equal to the post.

sentences.zh: 三年，吏民詣都上表，請立碑頌美功績，詔許之。

translations.literal: In the third year, officials and people went to the capital and submitted a memorial asking that a stele be erected to praise his achievements; an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the officials and people went to court with a memorial asking for a stele to honor his work. The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 太建元年，進號雲麾將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taijian he was advanced in title to Cloud-Banner General.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taijian (569) he was promoted to cloud-banner general.

sentences.zh: 二年卒，時年四十七。

translations.literal: In the second year he died, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year (570), at forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍，諡曰威。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant; his posthumous name was Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made scattered-cavalry regular attendant, with the posthumous name Wei.

sentences.zh: 子之武嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhiwu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhiwu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 之武年十六，領其舊軍，隨吳明徹北伐有功，官至王府主簿、弘農太守，仍隸明徹。

translations.literal: Zhiwu at sixteen led his father's old army; he followed Wu Mingche on the northern campaign with merit, rose to chief clerk of a princely establishment and Administrator of Hongnong, and still served under Mingche.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen Zhiwu took over his father's troops. He followed Wu Mingche north, earned merit, rose to a princely chief clerk and administrator of Hongnong, and remained under Mingche.

sentences.zh: 明徹於呂梁敗績，之武逃歸，為人所害，時年二十二。

translations.literal: When Mingche was defeated at Lüliang, Zhiwu fled home and was killed by others, aged twenty-two.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingche was broken at Lüliang, Zhiwu fled home and was murdered, aged twenty-two.

sentences.zh: 子隆弟子才，亦有幹略，從子隆征討有功，除南平太守，封始興縣子，[2]邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Zilong's younger brother's son Cai also had resource and plan; he followed Zilong on campaigns with merit, was made Administrator of Nanping, enfeoffed as Viscount of Shixing county, Editorial footnote marker 2. fief three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Zilong's nephew Cai had talent and nerve. He campaigned with Zilong, was made administrator of Nanping, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Shixing [2] with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 從吳明徹北伐，監安州，鎮于宿預。

translations.literal: He followed Wu Mingche on the northern campaign, supervised An province, and garrisoned at Suyu.
translations.idiomatic: He marched north with Wu Mingche, supervised An province, and held Suyu.

sentences.zh: 除中衛始興王諮議參軍，遷飆猛將軍、信州刺史。

translations.literal: He was made advisory military adjutant to the Central Guard Prince of Shixing, then transferred to Whirlwind Fierce General and Inspector of Xin.
translations.idiomatic: He became advisory military adjutant to the central guard prince of Shixing, then whirlwind-fierce general and inspector of Xin.

sentences.zh: 太建十三年卒，時年四十二。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Taijian he died, aged forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year of Taijian (581), at forty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Supernumerary Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 錢道戢字子韜，吳興長城人也。

translations.literal: Qian Daoji, styled Zitao, was a native of Changcheng in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Daoji, styled Zitao, came from Changcheng in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 父景深，梁漢壽令。

translations.literal: His father Jingshen was Liang magistrate of Hanshou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingshen had been magistrate of Hanshou under Liang.

sentences.zh: 道戢少以孝行著聞，及長，頗有幹略，高祖微時，以從妹妻焉。

translations.literal: Daoji in youth was famed for filial conduct; when grown he had considerable resource and plan; in the Founder's early days the Founder gave him a cousin in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji was known early for filial piety and, grown, showed real capacity. In the Founder's lean years the Founder married him to a cousin.

sentences.zh: 從平盧子略於廣州，除濱江令。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of Lu Zilue at Guangzhou and was made magistrate of Binjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in pacifying Lu Zilue at Guangzhou and was made magistrate of Binjiang.

sentences.zh: 高祖輔政，遣道戢隨世祖平張彪于會稽，以功拜直閤將軍，除員外散騎常侍、假節、東徐州刺史，封永安縣侯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: When the Founder acted as regent he sent Daoji to follow Emperor Wen in pacifying Zhang Biao at Kuaiji; for merit he was made Direct-Gate General, Supernumerary Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant with credentials, and Inspector of East Xuzhou, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yong'an with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: While the Founder held regency he sent Daoji with Emperor Wen to crush Zhang Biao at Kuaiji. For merit he was made direct-gate general, supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant with credentials, and inspector of East Xuzhou, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yong'an with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 仍領甲卒三千，隨侯安都鎮防梁山，尋領錢塘、餘杭二縣令。

translations.literal: He still led three thousand armored troops, followed Hou Andu to garrison and defend Liangshan, and soon also held the magistracies of Qiantang and Yuhang counties.
translations.idiomatic: He still commanded three thousand armored men, joined Hou Andu in garrisoning Liangshan, and soon held Qiantang and Yuhang as well.

sentences.zh: 永定三年，隨世祖鎮于南皖口。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongding he followed Emperor Wen in garrisoning at South Wan Ford.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongding (559) he followed Emperor Wen to garrison South Wan Ford.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，又領剡令，鎮于縣之南巖，尋為臨海太守，鎮巖如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjia he also held the magistracy of Shan, garrisoning at the county's Southern Cliff; soon he was made Administrator of Linhai, his garrison at the cliff unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjia (560) he added the magistracy of Shan and garrisoned the county's Southern Cliff. Soon he was made administrator of Linhai while keeping that post.

sentences.zh: 侯安都之討留異也，道戢帥軍出松陽以斷其後。

translations.literal: When Hou Andu campaigned against Liu Yi, Daoji led troops out through Songyang to cut his rear.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Andu attacked Liu Yi, Daoji marched through Songyang to sever his retreat.

sentences.zh: 異平，以功拜持節、通直散騎常侍、輕車將軍、都督東西二衡州諸軍事、衡州刺史，領始興內史。

translations.literal: When Yi was pacified, for merit he was made Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, Light-Carriage General, Commander of Military Affairs in the two Heng provinces east and west, and Inspector of Heng, concurrently Interior Administrator of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi was suppressed he received the staff, was made regular attendant of direct communication, light-carriage general, commander of the eastern and western Heng provinces, and inspector of Heng, and still held Shixing as interior administrator.

sentences.zh: 光大元年，增邑并前七百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangda his fief was increased together with the previous to seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangda (567) his fief was brought to seven hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 太建二年，又隨昭達征蕭巋於江陵，道戢別督眾軍與陸子隆焚青泥舟艦，仍為昭達前軍，攻安蜀城，降之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taijian he again followed Zhaoda in campaigning against Xiao Kui at Jiangling; Daoji separately commanded the massed armies with Lu Zilong to burn the green-mud fleet, then served as Zhaoda's vanguard, attacked Ancheng, and reduced it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taijian (570) he again followed Zhaoda against Xiao Kui at Jiangling. Daoji separately commanded the allied armies with Lu Zilong to burn the green-mud ships, then led Zhaoda's van, took Ancheng, and received its surrender.

sentences.zh: 以功加散騎常侍、仁武將軍，增邑并前九百戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced to Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant and Benevolent Martial General; his fief was increased together with the previous to nine hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant and benevolent-martial general, his fief rising to nine hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 其年，遷仁威將軍、吳興太守。

translations.literal: That year he was transferred to Benevolent Prestige General and Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was made benevolent-prestige general and administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 未行，改授使持節、都督郢巴武三州諸軍事、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post he was reassigned Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Military Affairs in the three provinces of Ying, Ba, and Wu, and Inspector of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Before he went out he was reassigned with the staff as commander of Ying, Ba, and Wu and inspector of Ying.

sentences.zh: 王師北討，道戢與儀同黃法𣰋圍歷陽。

translations.literal: When the imperial army marched north to campaign, Daoji with the yitong officer Huang Faqu besieged Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial troops marched north, Daoji and the yitong officer Huang Faqu besieged Liyang.

sentences.zh: 歷陽城平，因以道戢鎮之。

translations.literal: When Liyang city was pacified, Daoji was left to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: When Liyang fell he was left to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 以功加雲麾將軍，增邑并前一千五百戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced to Cloud-Banner General; his fief was increased together with the previous to one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was promoted to cloud-banner general, his fief brought to one thousand five hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月遘疾卒，時年六十三。

translations.literal: That year, in the eleventh month, he fell ill and died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: That year, in the eleventh month, he sickened and died, aged sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈本官，諡曰肅。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given his former office; his posthumous name was Su.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted his last office, with the posthumous name Su.

sentences.zh: 子邈嗣。

translations.literal: His son Miao inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Miao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 駱牙字旗門，[3]吳興臨安人也。

translations.literal: Luo Ya, styled Qimen, Editorial footnote marker 3. was a native of Lin'an in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Ya, styled Qimen, [3] came from Lin'an in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 祖祕道，梁安成王田曹參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Midao was Liang field-cadet in the Prince of Ancheng's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Midao had been field-cadet in the Prince of Ancheng's staff under Liang.

sentences.zh: 父裕，鄱陽嗣王中兵參軍事。

translations.literal: His father Yu was military adjutant of the central guard to the Prince of Poyang, heir to the kingship.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu was central-guard military adjutant to the Prince of Poyang, heir to the kingship.

sentences.zh: 牙年十二，宗人有善相者，云「此郎容貌非常，必將遠致」。

translations.literal: At twelve, a kinsman skilled in physiognomy said, "This boy's countenance is extraordinary; he will surely reach far."
translations.idiomatic: At twelve a clansman skilled in faces said, "This lad's looks are not ordinary. He will go far."

sentences.zh: 梁太清末，世祖嘗避地臨安，牙母陵，[4]睹世祖儀表，知非常人，賓待甚厚。

translations.literal: At the end of Liang's Taiping era Emperor Wen once took refuge at Lin'an; Ya's mother Ling, Editorial footnote marker 4. saw Emperor Wen's bearing, knew he was no ordinary man, and entertained him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Liang's Taiping era Emperor Wen once sheltered at Lin'an. Ya's mother Ling [4] saw his bearing, knew he was no common man, and received him with deep courtesy.

sentences.zh: 及世祖為吳興太守，引牙為將帥，因從平杜龕、張彪等，每戰輒先鋒陷陣，[5]勇冠眾軍，以功授直閤將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen became Administrator of Wuxing he took Ya on as a commander; Ya followed him in pacifying Du Kan, Zhang Biao, and others; in every battle he always took the van and broke the line, Editorial footnote marker 5. his courage topped all the armies; for merit he was made Direct-Gate General.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen became administrator of Wuxing he made Ya a commander. Ya followed him against Du Kan, Zhang Biao, and the rest, always first through the breach; [5] his bravery outshone every unit. For merit he was made direct-gate general.

sentences.zh: 太平二年，以母憂去職。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping he left office for his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping (557) he left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 世祖鎮會稽，起為山陰令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen garrisoned Kuaiji he was recalled to serve as magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen held Kuaiji he was recalled as magistrate of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 永定三年，除安東府中兵參軍，出鎮冶城。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongding he was made military adjutant of the central guard in the Pacifying East establishment and went out to garrison Yecheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongding (559) he was made central-guard military adjutant in the pacifying-east staff and went out to hold Yecheng.

sentences.zh: 尋從世祖拒王琳於南皖。

translations.literal: Soon he followed Emperor Wen in resisting Wang Lin at South Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he followed Emperor Wen against Wang Lin at South Wan.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，授假節、威虜將軍、員外散騎常侍，封常安縣侯，[6]邑五百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne he was given credentials, made Might-Subduing General and Supernumerary Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, enfeoffed as Marquis of Chang'an county, Editorial footnote marker 6. fief five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded he was given credentials as might-subduing general and supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Chang'an [6] with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋為臨安令，遷越州刺史，餘並如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was made magistrate of Lin'an, then transferred to Inspector of Yue; the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was magistrate of Lin'an, then inspector of Yue, his other titles unchanged.

sentences.zh: 初，牙母之卒也，于時飢饉兵荒，至是始葬，詔贈牙母常安國太夫人，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ya's mother died, famine and war raged; only now was she buried; an edict posthumously honored Ya's mother as Grand Madam of Chang'an state, posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother had died, famine and war made burial impossible. Only now was she laid to rest. An edict posthumously honored her as Grand Madam of Chang'an state, with the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 遷牙為貞威將軍、晉陵太守。

translations.literal: Ya was transferred to Faithful Prestige General and Administrator of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Ya was made faithful-prestige general and administrator of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 三年，以平周迪之功，遷冠軍將軍、臨川內史。

translations.literal: In the third year, for merit in pacifying Zhou Di, he was transferred to Champion General and Interior Administrator of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, for pacifying Zhou Di, he was made champion general and interior administrator of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 太建三年，授安遠將軍、衡陽內史，未拜，徙為桂陽太守。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taijian he was given Pacifying Distance General and Interior Administrator of Hengyang; before he took up the post he was moved to Administrator of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taijian (572) he was made pacifying-distance general and interior administrator of Hengyang. Before he went out he was shifted to administrator of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 八年，還朝，遷散騎常侍，入直殿省。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he returned to court and was transferred to Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, entering direct service in the palace offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (577) he returned to court as scattered-cavalry regular attendant on duty in the palace offices.

sentences.zh: 十年，授豐州刺史，餘並如故。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was given Inspector of Feng; the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (579) he was made inspector of Feng, his other titles unchanged.

sentences.zh: 至德二年卒，時年五十七。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide he died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Zhide (584), at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈安遠將軍、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Pacifying Distance General and Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made pacifying-distance general and inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 子義嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：陸子隆、錢道戢，或舉門願從，或舊齒樹勳，有統領之才，充師旅之寄。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Lu Zilong and Qian Daoji—one brought his whole household to follow, the other was an old companion who raised merit from the first—both had talent to command and were fit to bear the army's trust.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Lu Zilong and Qian Daoji—one brought his house to follow, one stood with the Founder from the first—both could lead and were trusted with the armies.

sentences.zh: 至於受任藩屏，功績並著，美矣！

translations.literal: As to receiving border appointments and achieving merit together—how fine!
translations.idiomatic: Given frontier command and shared achievement—how fine indeed!

sentences.zh: 駱牙識真有奉，知世祖天授之德，蓋張良之亞歟？

translations.literal: Luo Ya recognized true worth and served it; he knew Emperor Wen's heaven-granted virtue—was he not next to Zhang Liang?
translations.idiomatic: Luo Ya saw true worth and served it; he knew Emperor Wen bore heaven's mandate—was he not Zhang Liang's peer?

sentences.zh: 牙母智深先覺，符柏谷之禮，君子知鑒識弘遠，其在茲乎！

translations.literal: Ya's mother, wise and foreseeing, matched the rite of Bo Valley; the gentleman knows that keen judgment reaching far—was it not here?
translations.idiomatic: Ya's mother, wise before the fact, matched the courtesy of Bo Valley. A gentleman will say that vision reaching far lived here.

sentences.zh: 〔柵〕口 「沌口」當作「柵口」，今改正。

translations.literal: [Zha] mouth—"Dunkou" should read "Zhakou"; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: [Zha] mouth—"Dunkou" should read "Zhakou"; emended now.

translations.literal: For details see Chapter 11
translations.idiomatic: For details see Chapter 11

translations.literal: 〈Biography of Zhaoda〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Biography of Zhaoda〉

sentences.zh: 校記五。

translations.literal: Collation note five.
translations.idiomatic: Collation note five.

sentences.zh: 封始興縣子 「始興」《南史》作「始康」。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed as Viscount of Shixing county—"Shixing" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Shikang."
translations.idiomatic: On "enfeoffed as Viscount of Shixing county": the History of the Southern Dynasties reads Shikang.

sentences.zh: 駱牙字旗門 「駱牙」《南史》作「駱文牙」。

translations.literal: Luo Ya styled Qimen—"Luo Ya" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Luo Wenya."
translations.idiomatic: On "Luo Ya styled Qimen": the History of the Southern Dynasties reads Luo Wenya.

sentences.zh: 牙母陵 「陵」殿本作「陳」。

translations.literal: Ya's mother Ling—"Ling" in the Hall edition reads "Chen."
translations.idiomatic: On "Ya's mother Ling": the Hall edition reads Chen.

sentences.zh: 考證云「『陳』各本俱誤『陵』，今從《南史》。」

translations.literal: Textual verification says "'Chen' is corrupt as 'Ling' in all editions; now follows the History of the Southern Dynasties."
translations.idiomatic: Textual verification holds that Chen is corrupt for Ling in all editions; the text now follows the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 每戰輒先鋒陷陣 「輒」字原本缺，據各本補。

translations.literal: In every battle always took the van—"always" (zhe) was missing in the original and is supplied from the various editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "in every battle always took the van": zhe (always) was missing in the base text and is restored from other editions.

sentences.zh: 封常安縣侯 按「常安」當從《南史》作「臨安」。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed as Marquis of Chang'an county—by examination "Chang'an" should follow the History of the Southern Dynasties and read "Lin'an."
translations.idiomatic: On "enfeoffed as Marquis of Chang'an county": examination shows Chang'an should follow the History of the Southern Dynasties as Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 下「常安國」亦當從《南史》作「臨安國」。

translations.literal: Below, "Chang'an state" should likewise follow the History of the Southern Dynasties and read "Lin'an state."
translations.idiomatic: Below, "Chang'an state" should likewise follow the History of the Southern Dynasties as Lin'an state.
